problem.text: The architecture registry lacked DeciLMForCausalLM. The existing Llama constructor uses uniform attention and MLP settings, whereas the new adapter constructs branches and widths from per-block configuration.

reasoning.text: The implementation reuses shared transformer modules rather than introducing a separate execution kernel, preserving familiar checkpoint names while allowing heterogeneous blocks.

impact.text: Config.from_directory can now dispatch DeciLMForCausalLM to DeciLMConfig. This establishes architecture selection and construction logic, not verified compatibility with every Nemotron checkpoint.

source_notes.text: Whole-parent searches found no Nemotron occurrence; Deci matches were unrelated calibration prose. The inspected discussion reports concern a native-extension symbol error, Qwen chat stop conditions, and missing-BOS tokenization, rather than reporting DeciLM support.

limitations: No DeciLM checkpoint configuration, tensor header, reference implementation or model execution was available to establish checkpoint or numerical equivalence.

The width check is a Python scalar transcription, not repository model execution or a GPU test. The architectural rationale for the 2/3 multiplier and 256-wide alignment is not established by the inspected sources.
Conversion, generation quality and performance were not tested.

chapters.title: DeciLM dispatch and heterogeneous block construction

claims.text: The earlier architecture entry describes dispatch and checkpoint mapping through shared modules. This change extends that design with a dedicated DeciLM configuration and model pair.

DeciLMConfig requires block_configs to contain exactly num_hidden_layers entries. It retains global hidden width and query-head count, derives head_dim by integer division when absent or false, accepts SiLU or an omitted hidden_act, and requests the shared NEOX-style RoPE settings.

Each block reads attention and ffn dictionaries. A truthy no_op omits that branch and its norm; otherwise attention receives n_heads_in_group as num_kv_heads, while the MLP receives a block-specific intermediate width. Shared TransformerBlock.forward conditionally executes present branches with residual additions.

Active attention branches reject sink-token, linear-replacement, sparsification, unshifted-sink and prefill-window-in-sink options through assertions; active FFNs reject linear replacement and sparsification. These checks occur after the no_op decision, so omitted branches bypass them.
MLP width is computed as int(2 * ffn_mult * hidden_size / 3), then rounded upward to a multiple of 256 using an added 255 before integer division. Truncation therefore precedes alignment.

A scalar transcription produced widths 11008 for hidden_size=4096 and ffn_mult=4, 8192 for 4096 and 3, and 768 for 1024 and 1. Exhaustively checking intermediate integers 1 through 100000 confirmed that alignment returns a multiple of 256 no smaller than its input and adds fewer than 256 elements.

Checkpoint layer numbering remains the original block index, but attention layer_idx advances only for present attention branches. last_kv_module_idx tracks the latest attention-containing block. This separates checkpoint positions from compact cache indexing; the existing Cache constructor allocates one cache layer per model.get_cache_layers() entry rather than per configured hidden layer.

The adapter retains model.embed_tokens, separate q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj and gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj names, final model.norm and lm_head. It preserves the tied-embedding alternate-key logic, marks the head as logits output, and delegates input preparation to prepare_for_attn.

annotation.summary: Adds DeciLM architecture dispatch and per-block attention/MLP construction, including optional branches, variable widths and compact cache indices; checkpoint compatibility remains untested.
